source_text: Tu sane nostrum vexando silentium, protulisti quod olim quidem defendi non potuit; nunc vero postquam Manichaei epistola, cuius in libro tertio sententias posui, venit ad publicum, nec celari potest.
pass_a_gloss: You, to be sure, by harassing our silence, have brought forth what indeed of old could not be defended; but now, after the letter of Manichaeus, whose sentences I set down in the third book, has come to the public, it cannot even be hidden.

lemmas.lexica: Blaise Manichaeus; Julian's polemic label vs natural evil
LS/Blaise range; English follows the Latin without NPNF copy

pass_b_english: Indeed, by harassing my silence, you have brought out something that could never be defended before, and that now cannot even be concealed, since Manichaeus’s letter, passages from which I quoted in the third book, has become public.

choices.why: Julian's standing charge: natural evil is Manichaean. Keep the sect-name, not 'dualists'.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
